content: Individuals with diabetes are at an increased risk of developing infections. Therefore, it is highly recommended that they receive routine vaccinations to reduce this risk. 1. Vaccination Schedules: It is essential to adhere to the vaccination schedules outlined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), ensuring that age-appropriate immunizations are administered. These include vaccines for influenza, pneumococcal disease, hepatitis B, and COVID-19. 2. Personalized Recommendations: Healthcare providers should customize vaccination plans based on the individual’s specific characteristics, such as their age, overall health condition, and the presence of any additional medical conditions (comorbidities).
